suggestion: Put the decision on the landing page instead of the summary: today's slate, the desk's number, the market's number, the difference, and what the gate says about acting on it.
options: A: restructure index.html around the line sheet. B: keep the executive summary and add a four-number decision strip above it. C: leave as is.
cost: A: about an hour, moves one table up. B: fifteen minutes, adds one block. C: nothing.
what_changes: The first thing a reviewer reads changes from 'what we did' to 'what the numbers say right now'. No table content moves.
recommendation: B - the decision strip is the part that gets used; the summary still needs to exist for the provenance.

suggestion: Show the model's uncertainty next to every difference (in ticks of the 0.5 point), so a 1-tick disagreement and a 6-tick disagreement do not look like the same kind of event.
options: A: add a ticks column (already computed). B: add a shaded band instead of a number. C: add both, number in the table and band in the chart.
cost: A: trivial, the column exists in data/line_sheet.csv. B: needs a chart, about an hour. C: both.
what_changes: Readers can dismiss sub-tick disagreement without being told to; currently the table invites treating 0.5 and 4.5 the same.
recommendation: A now, B only if someone will actually read a chart.

suggestion: Freeze the strategy list for a fixed period (say six weeks) and publish the freeze date, so the board measures strategies rather than measuring how fast we can re-tune them.
options: A: hard freeze, no new variants for six weeks. B: new variants allowed but they enter the competition only at the next freeze. C: status quo.
cost: A and B: a policy, not code - plus one column in multiplicity.csv. C: nothing.
what_changes: Every p-value on the board becomes interpretable: multiplicity correction over a closed set is meaningful, over an open one it is theatre.
recommendation: B: it keeps exploration free while making the scoreboard honest.

suggestion: Publish the injury ladder as a per-position table joined to snap share, and delete any presentation that implies a player-level 'will he play' prediction.
options: A: replace the status list with the position-level table. B: keep both, clearly split. C: status quo.
cost: A: small render change. B: no change to data, one more section.
what_changes: Removes the most-abused number on any NFL desk page. The base rate (Questionable played 58.6% of 590 player-weeks) stays as context and stops being used as a player forecast.

suggestion: Add a 'price of the absence' column that is explicitly unpriced where the replacement is UNTESTED, rather than defaulting to a league-average replacement.
options: A: blank cell plus a warning glyph, as now - formalise it. B: show a league-average value in a separate, clearly labelled 'what-if' column. C: hide untested rows.
cost: A: documentation only. B: one derived column and a rule for it.
what_changes: Decides what the desk admits to not knowing. C is the wrong answer: hiding a row hides the fact that it was hidden.
recommendation: B, with the what-if column never used in any gate or leaderboard number.

suggestion: Run the capture job twice per game-day (at kickoff and 30 minutes before) so the closing stage exists from the next live week onward.
options: A: two scheduled runs per slate day. B: hourly on game days. C: one run.
cost: A: schedule entries plus a re-run guard. B: more rows, more noise, no new information beyond A for closing purposes.
what_changes: Unblocks gate V-08 (CLV) and rule D3 in the demotion gate - both are currently blocked by data, not by method. Roughly 20-30 closing rows per week.

suggestion: Print the refusal table (correlations the desk will not compute) beside the values it does print, not in a separate appendix.
options: A: one table, refusals as rows with blank r and a reason. B: two tables.
cost: Trivial - the rows already exist in data/correlations.csv.
what_changes: A reviewer can see what is missing without hunting, which is how a missing correlation stops being mistaken for a zero one.
recommendation: A, already implemented in the data; the page layout needs the same choice.

suggestion: Publish a per-season table (2021-2025) beside the pooled one, since a pooled average over five seasons is dominated by whichever year the model happened to like.
options: A: add season rows to the signal table. B: separate page. C: skip.
cost: Small: the rows carry a season column already.
what_changes: Stability becomes visible: a signal present in 2 of 5 seasons reads differently from one present in 5 of 5, and today the board cannot show that.

suggestion: Make 'no source link, no row' a machine-checked rule with a named exception list, rather than a convention the builder follows.
options: A: verify.py fails the build on any table row lacking a source column value or an explicit blank-and-flag marker. B: keep it as a convention.
cost: A: one check in verify.py plus an exceptions file.
what_changes: A convention breaks the first time someone is in a hurry; a check does not.
recommendation: A. The exception list is where an unavoidable gap gets argued about in the open.

suggestion: Decide whether this desk's product is a decision tool or an evidence archive, and drop the half that is not chosen.
options: A: decision tool - the archive moves behind a 'how we know' link. B: archive - the decision strip loses its prominence. C: both, and accept that it does neither well.
cost: A layout and tone decision, no compute.
what_changes: Everything: it decides what a reader sees first, what gets refreshed, and what is allowed to be stale.
recommendation: A. Lines rot in hours; archives do not.
